title: Two Songpals One Mic
style: acoustic singer-songwriter, fingerpicked nylon guitar, light upright bass, soft brushed snare, warm male and female duet, intimate room sound, 84 bpm, conversational, tender
lyrics:
[Verse 1 - Male]
I brought a notebook full of half-things
Lines that didn't know where to go
You brought a melody you whistled
Walking home in last week's snow

[Verse 2 - Female]
You put your half-things on the table
I hummed mine into the air
We pieced together something fragile
In a kitchen, in a chair

[Chorus - Both]
Two songpals, one microphone
Making a small thing of our own
No charts to chase, no crowd to please
Just a melody between the trees
Two songpals, one little song
Quiet enough to carry along

[Verse 3 - Male]
You changed a word and made it true
I changed a chord and made it bend
We stayed up until the streetlights
Became the morning, then a friend

[Chorus - Both]
Two songpals, one microphone
Making a small thing of our own
No charts to chase, no crowd to please
Just a melody between the trees
Two songpals, one little song
Quiet enough to carry along

[Bridge - Female]
The world can have its anthems
The world can have its noise
We'll keep this little chorus
For the people we love, and the quiet joys

[Outro - Both, harmony]
Two songpals, one mic
Two songpals, one mic
Two songpals, one mic
Goodnight, goodnight
